verdicts.critic:
STEELMAN REVIEW — "AI Alignment Approaches" (9 positions)

Verdict: one blocking defect, in Control Engineer. Everything else on my dimension holds at or above published parity.

POSITION-BY-POSITION ENDORSEMENT TEST

1. Iterative Empiricist — would endorse. Leads with the camp's own strongest empirical card (InstructGPT 1.3B beating untuned 175B, verified against Ouyang et al.), gives the strategic argument in Schulman's and Anthropic's own words (both quotes verified: Schulman's "big buildup in potential energy" from the Dwarkesh interview; Anthropic Core Views' "excessive caution … only ever engage with systems that are far behind the frontier"), and answers the killer objection rather than ducking it ("no rival program has cleared that higher bar either"). Names its own internal split (how much of the loop to hand to RLAIF).

2. Internals Auditor — would endorse, and notably it is sourced from the camp's own texts rather than its critics. The auditing-game account is accurate at team-level granularity: I checked Marks et al. team by team — Teams 1 and 2 used SAEs, Team 3 was barred from SAEs and got there via prefill attacks plus keyword search of the corpus, Team 4 had API access only and failed. The draft even carries the paper's own honest caveat that SAE features sometimes amount to "a convenient interface for semantic search" while outperforming that baseline in other cases. Nanda's pivot is quoted correctly ("Swiss cheese", pragmatic interpretability).

3. Control Engineer — would endorse the argument, but one sentence in the description is factually wrong about a live document and would embarrass the camp. See blocking. The quantitative core is verified exactly (5,000-problem APPS runs, 2% human-audit budget, trusted monitoring 62% → 8%/38% framing correct), as is the three-month SaferAI external review of DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Pro scheming-inability safety case, including the human-oversight failure-mode list (automation bias, alert fatigue, time pressure, manipulation, volumes beyond review capacity, common-mode correlation).

4. Oversight Amplifier — would endorse. Correct genealogy (IDA, debate, RRM, all 2018), the camp's best result (Engels et al. debate 51.7% at a 400-Elo gap against 13.5/10.0/9.4 — verified verbatim from the abstract), and the camp's own unresolved worry (obfuscated arguments) stated by the camp rather than by an opponent.

5. Value Pluralist — would endorse. Gabriel's reflective-endorsement framing, Lazar's monoculture/legitimacy critique and the CCAI ~50% overlap all check out against the primary sources, and the camp's claim is put at its strongest ("every training method quietly answers the whose-values question already"). One structural asymmetry noted below.

6. Alignment Pessimist — would endorse. It gives the camp its concrete ask (halt until verification exists), its founding fact (MIRI's own reversal), its two internal mechanisms (Yampolskiy's in-principle case vs Yudkowsky/Soares' empirical one), and the strongest available evidence base, with the crucial rhetorical point that the findings came from labs with the opposite incentive. The signature count (72,233) I confirmed live today, and it is dated in-text.

7. Provable Safety Engineer — would endorse. It reports the February 2026 ARIA narrowing honestly rather than hiding it, which is what makes the camp credible rather than weaker; the £59m, the two-TA refocus, the dropped cyber-physical phase-2 call and davidad's April 2026 move to technical advisor all verified on ARIA's own page.

8. Tool AI Architect — would endorse. Aguirre's A/G/I intersection, the 10^27 FLOP training cap and 10^20 FLOP/s inference cap, and strict liability are all as proposed; the camp's own hardest objection (a bounded system loses to an unbounded one) is stated and answered in-voice.

9. Multi-Agent Safety Researcher — would endorse. Verified: 42 co-authors on the CAIF report, the exact three failure modes and seven risk factors, and the $10m call's premise. The camp is even given its own hardest open problem (no frontier multi-agent failure yet demonstrated that cannot be redescribed as one component being misaligned) without that concession being used to undercut it.

NO HOUSE VERDICT, NO FALSE BALANCE. Prevalence runs 80 → 20 rather than flattening, the crux lists nine distinct standards of proof without ranking them, and the asymmetry is carried by shared Basics facts that each camp reads its own way (the draft says so explicitly in the Basics intro and in the Engels detail: "the finding cuts both ways and both sides cite it").

NO STRAWMEN FOUND. No camp is sourced from its opponents' characterisation; each is sourced from its own authoritative texts and named proponents. The one camp that could easily have been strawmanned — Alignment Pessimist — is instead given the strongest empirical version of its case rather than the caricatured one.

MISSING CAMPS: I searched for a major absent position and found none that blocks. The closest candidates are (a) theory-first agent foundations (MIRI's original agenda, ARC's ELK/heuristic-arguments line) and (b) the alignment-optimist/default-alignment camp. (a) is largely represented through Alignment Pessimist's people and Provable Safety Engineer's methods; (b) is given a real, in-voice hearing in Q1 via Belrose and Pope, whose argument I verified verbatim against their own post, and much of it falls under scope_excluded ("how likely AI catastrophe is").

blocking.issue: Misstates what Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy currently requires. RSP v3.0 (effective 2026-02-24, the version in force) does NOT require an affirmative misalignment safety case as a shipping gate. Its "affirmative case" language applies to capability-threshold testing ("we now require an affirmative case that models are sufficiently far from Capability Thresholds"). The misalignment/sabotage bar — "A frontier developer should make a strong argument that AI systems will not carry out sabotage leading to irreversibly and substantially higher odds of a later global catastrophe" — sits in the "ambitious industry-wide recommendations" column, which v3.0 explicitly separates from company commitments: "we cannot commit to following them unilaterally." Anthropic's own commitment in that row is to detail capabilities, propensities, monitoring and overall risk in Risk Reports. The claim was true of RSP v2.1 (March 2025), which required an affirmative case on misalignment risk past the AI R&D-4 threshold, but the draft asserts it in the present tense. This is the sentence carrying the camp's "it is now industry policy, not aspiration" argument, so an opponent could knock out the camp's strongest institutional evidence on a factual error. The Google DeepMind half of the sentence is correct (FSF safety-case reviews before external launch once a critical capability level is reached) and should stay.

prevalence_basis.name: Iterative Empiricist
prevalence_basis.prevalence_basis: The documented production method behind every deployed frontier model (RLHF, Constitutional AI, deliberative alignment), and treated as the state of the art in the February 2026 International AI Safety Report.
prevalence_basis.sketch: Alignment is an empirical engineering problem: train on human and model-generated feedback, measure the failures, patch, and repeat, the way every shipped frontier model is already built.

prevalence_basis.name: Internals Auditor
prevalence_basis.prevalence_basis: Dedicated interpretability teams at Anthropic, Google DeepMind and OpenAI, a standing mechanistic-interpretability workshop track at ICML and NeurIPS, and a named core area of the UK AISI Alignment Project agenda.
prevalence_basis.sketch: Behavior can be faked, so trust has to rest on reading a model’s internal computation; interpretability must mature into a reliable audit before systems are handed real autonomy.

prevalence_basis.name: Control Engineer
prevalence_basis.prevalence_basis: Written into frontier safety frameworks and safety-case practice; joint UK AISI and Redwood Research control work, and one of the two headline questions in the Alignment Project’s agenda.
prevalence_basis.sketch: Assume the system may be misaligned and engineer so it cannot cause harm anyway: layered monitoring, restricted affordances, and safety cases that no single technique has to carry alone.

prevalence_basis.name: Oversight Amplifier
prevalence_basis.prevalence_basis: A long-running research program at Google DeepMind, Anthropic and OpenAI, and a named priority area (debate, amplified oversight, recursive reward modeling) in the UK AISI Alignment Project’s over-£15 million research agenda.
prevalence_basis.sketch: Human judgment is the bottleneck, so use AI to extend it: debate, task decomposition and recursive reward modeling let weak supervisors grade work they could not check themselves.

prevalence_basis.name: Value Pluralist
prevalence_basis.prevalence_basis: Sustained presence in FAccT and NeurIPS pluralistic-alignment venues and in social-choice and participatory norm-elicitation literature; largely academic rather than embedded in lab deployment practice.
prevalence_basis.sketch: The unsolved part is not control but legitimacy: whose values a system encodes, and by what process that gets decided, is a question no training method answers.

prevalence_basis.name: Alignment Pessimist
prevalence_basis.prevalence_basis: Backed by advocacy organizations (MIRI, ControlAI, PauseAI) and a widely reviewed 2025 trade book; a small share of technical research output, a much larger share of public and policy debate.
prevalence_basis.sketch: None of the current programs verifies what a grown system actually wants, so frontier scaling should stop until one of them does.

prevalence_basis.name: Provable Safety Engineer
prevalence_basis.prevalence_basis: Backed by the UK ARIA Safeguarded AI program and Bengio’s LawZero, and endorsed by senior figures (Bengio, Russell, Tegmark); a small researcher base with no working prototypes as of early 2026.
prevalence_basis.sketch: Empirical testing cannot bound behavior; safety should come from formal specifications, world models and proof certificates checked before anything is deployed.

prevalence_basis.name: Deployment Witness
prevalence_basis.prevalence_basis: An established peer-reviewed field (FAccT, AIES) rather than a single lab’s position, backed by an independent institute (DAIR, founded 2021) and widely cited primary texts — Stochastic Parrots and the SMACTR audit framework among them — smaller in headcount than reliability-focused ML safety work but institutionally entrenched, and named as one of the field’s three organizing camps in a 2026 arXiv position paper (Jha, Svarc and Bagiński).
prevalence_basis.sketch: Alignment is judged by deployed systems’ documented effects on the people subject to them, not by pre-deployment verification of hypothetical takeover.
